name: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (TNNI3)
description: A heart-muscle disease in which the wall of the left ventricle thickens abnormally; in the Golden Retriever family where it was found, affected puppies died suddenly before two years of age. Recessive.

name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease 1J with amelogenesis imperfecta
description: A combination of poorly formed, easily worn tooth enamel and slowed nerve conduction (a mild peripheral neuropathy), described in Lancashire Heelers. Recessive.

name: Progressive retinal atrophy (GTPBP2)
description: A form of progressive retinal atrophy, in which the light-sensing cells of the retina degenerate and vision is gradually lost; found in a Labrador Retriever family. Recessive.

name: Hypothyroidism and dwarfism
description: Thyroglobulin deficiency: the thyroid cannot make normal hormone, causing dwarfism, limb deformities, thick skin and slow development in puppies. Described in Rottweilers. Recessive.

name: Bifid nose
description: The split (double) nose that is a hallmark of the Turkish Çatalburun breed; a physical trait, not a disease.

name: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy (GJC2)
description: A disorder of the brain's nerve insulation (myelin) causing head and body tremors from birth; described in Toy Poodles. Recessive.

name: Progressive retinal atrophy, Miniature Schnauzer, type 1
description: A form of progressive retinal atrophy in Miniature Schnauzers: the retina gradually degenerates, with night blindness first and later loss of day vision. Recessive.

name: Neuroaxonal dystrophy (RNF170)
description: A slowly progressive degeneration of nerve fibres causing hind-limb weakness and an unsteady gait in young adult dogs; described in Miniature American Shepherds. Recessive.

name: Polioencephalopathy
description: An inherited metabolic brain disease causing early-onset movement disorders (unsteady gait, abnormal limb movements) in young Eurasier dogs. Recessive.

name: Cerebellar cortical degeneration, granuloprival
description: Degeneration of the cerebellum (the brain's coordination centre) causing a progressive wobbly gait and head tremors in puppies. Reported in a single mixed-breed dog with one copy of a new (de novo) variant.

name: Mannosidosis, alpha
description: A lysosomal storage disease: a missing sugar-processing enzyme lets waste build up in cells, causing progressive neurological decline in young dogs. Reported in a Doberman Pinscher. Recessive.

name: Leigh syndrome
description: A mitochondrial energy disorder of the brain causing progressive unsteadiness and abnormal muscle tone in puppies; found in a Jack Russell Terrier x Chihuahua litter. Recessive.

name: Hypomyelinating polyneuropathy (MTMR2)
description: A congenital disorder of the insulation around peripheral nerves, causing weakness from a young age; described in Golden Retrievers. Recessive.

name: Glycogen storage disease myopathy
description: Abnormal glycogen (sugar store) builds up in heart and other muscles; described in young adult Basset Hounds. Recessive.

name: Paw pad hyperkeratosis (GJB6)
description: Thickened, hard paw pads on all feet. Reported in a single Labrador Retriever with one copy of a new (de novo) variant.

name: GST-theta enzyme deficiency (drug metabolism)
description: Low activity of a liver detoxifying enzyme (GSTT5). Not a disease, but dogs with two copies may process some drugs and chemicals differently; common in Beagles and Pembroke Welsh Corgis. Recessive.

name: Dilated cardiomyopathy and sudden death (ABCC9)
description: An inherited heart-muscle disease in which puppies can die suddenly; found in Manchester Terriers. Recessive with complete penetrance: dogs with two copies are affected.

name: Addison's disease and multiple autoimmune syndrome
description: Juvenile-onset Addison's disease (adrenal gland failure), often with other autoimmune problems, in Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers. Recessive; about three in four dogs with two copies develop early-onset disease.

name: Degenerative encephalopathy
description: A slowly progressive brain disease of Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers, with violent movements during sleep, anxiety, noise sensitivity and later cognitive and gait problems. Recessive.

name: Myopathy, creatine deficiency (GATM)
description: A muscle disease caused by a lack of creatine, with muscle wasting, exercise intolerance and an enlarged oesophagus; in the reported family, signs improved with creatine supplements. Recessive.

name: Slow drug metabolism (CYP1A2)
description: Dogs with two copies lack a working CYP1A2 liver enzyme and clear certain drugs slowly. Not a disease, but worth sharing with your vet; first found in Beagles. Recessive.

name: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (CASR)
description: Persistently high blood calcium with low calcium in the urine, caused by a faulty calcium-sensing receptor; reported in a Border Collie cross. Knowing about it can spare a dog unnecessary parathyroid surgery. Recessive.

name: Factor XIII deficiency
description: A rare bleeding disorder in which blood clots are unstable, causing spontaneous or prolonged bleeding; reported in a Black and Tan Coonhound. Recessive.

name: Ichthyosis, syndromic (DSP)
description: Generalised scaly, thickened skin with paw pad, hair and tooth abnormalities. Reported in a single Miniature Poodle with one copy of a new (de novo) variant.

name: Ichthyosis, ALOXE3-related
description: An inherited skin disorder with generalised scaling from puppyhood; reported in a Chihuahua. Recessive.

name: Congenital myasthenic syndrome (AGRN)
description: A disorder of the nerve-muscle junction behind 'dancing Doberman' and 'duck walking' gaits: hind-limb weakness, muscle wasting and fatigue in Doberman Pinschers. Recessive.

name: Immunodeficiency, CARMIL2-related
description: An inherited immune deficiency causing pneumonia (including Pneumocystis), gut and skin disease; found in Cavalier King Charles Spaniels. Recessive.

name: Cirneco oculo-neurological syndrome
description: Retinal degeneration together with tremors and episodes resembling seizures; described in Cirneco dell'Etna dogs. Recessive.

name: Paroxysmal exercise-induced dyskinesia
description: Episodes of muscle stiffness and abnormal movement triggered by exercise or stress, in Shetland Sheepdogs. Dominant: one copy can cause it.

name: PCYT2 deficiency
description: A disorder of cell-membrane fat production causing progressive retinal, brain and nerve degeneration; described in Saarloos Wolfdogs. Recessive.

name: Lysosomal storage disease, CNP-related
description: A slowly progressive neurological disease of adult Weimaraners, with incoordination, weakness and cognitive decline.

name: Mycobacterium avium susceptibility (CARD9)
description: An immune deficiency that leaves dogs vulnerable to systemic infection with Mycobacterium avium, a germ that rarely harms other dogs; found in Miniature Schnauzers. Recessive.

name: Ataxia, SETX-related
description: A slowly progressive stiff, high-stepping gait in an adult Jack Russell Terrier. Recessive.

name: Phloiokeratosis
description: Patches of thick, tree-bark-like skin. X-linked: one copy can cause it in females (often in streaks along the body) and males with the variant are affected.

name: Progressive retinal atrophy, X-linked (CACNA1F)
description: An X-linked form of progressive retinal atrophy in English Cocker Spaniels: affected males lose vision from about 3-4 years of age; females with one copy are carriers.

name: Spastic ataxia (SACS)
description: A progressive degeneration of the brain, spinal cord and nerves causing incoordination and stiffness from a few months of age; described in Great Pyrenees. Recessive.

name: Hairlessness (canine ectodermal dysplasia)
description: The variant that makes Chinese Crested, Peruvian Hairless and Xoloitzcuintli dogs hairless, often with missing teeth. One copy gives the hairless type; two copies are thought to be lethal before birth, so hairless dogs carry one copy.

name: Juvenile paroxysmal dyskinesia (SOD1)
description: A severe neurological disease of puppies (weakness, cramping and falling) found in the Markiesje (Dutch Tulip Hound). Different from degenerative myelopathy, which involves another SOD1 variant. Recessive.

name: GAPO syndrome
description: Growth retardation, hair loss, unerupted teeth and eye abnormalities, including glaucoma; described in Segugio Italiano dogs. Recessive.

name: Anemia with spinocerebellar ataxia
description: Progressive incoordination with retinal degeneration and severe anemia; reported in a single mixed-breed dog. Recessive.

name: Bilateral anterior amelia
description: Puppies born without front legs; described in Chihuahuas. Recessive. The screen reads the three linked variants reported for it.

name: Primary hyperparathyroidism (Keeshond)
description: Overactive parathyroid glands raising blood calcium, usually in older Keeshonden (over 8 years); treatable once found. Dominant with high age-related penetrance: one copy raises the risk.

name: Bald thigh syndrome (risk)
description: Hair loss on the thighs of sighthounds such as Greyhounds and Whippets. The variant is a risk factor found in nearly all Greyhounds; cosmetic, not painful.

name: Protein-losing nephropathy (KIRREL2 component, with NPHS1)
description: A kidney disease in which protein leaks into the urine, mostly in adult Soft-Coated Wheaten Terriers. This variant is one of two linked risk markers (with NPHS1); risk is highest with two copies of both.

name: Pituitary-dependent Cushing's disease risk (CRHR1)
description: A risk marker for pituitary-dependent hyperadrenocorticism (Cushing's disease: excess cortisol causing thirst, appetite and coat changes), found in Poodles. Raises risk; not a diagnosis.

name: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (TNXB)
description: A connective-tissue disorder with fragile, overly stretchy skin that tears easily; found in Chihuahuas and Poodles. Recessive.

name: Goniodysgenesis and glaucoma (OLFML3)
description: Malformed drainage angle of the eye (pectinate ligament dysplasia) that can lead to painful, sight-threatening glaucoma; found in Border Collies. Recessive.

name: Biliverdinuria
description: Life-long green urine caused by a missing bile-pigment enzyme; reported in mixed-breed dogs. Usually harmless on its own. Recessive.

name: Congenital microphthalmos with hematopoietic defects
description: Small eyes from birth together with stunted growth, enamel defects, anemia and low platelets; found in Portuguese Water Dogs. Recessive.

name: Congenital mirror movement disorder 1
description: Puppies move their legs in synchrony (a hopping, 'bunny hop' gait) instead of alternating; described in Weimaraners. Recessive.

name: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
description: Defective removal of immune cells, causing enlarged lymph nodes and spleen and low blood-cell counts in young Boerboels. Recessive.

name: Marfan syndrome
description: A connective-tissue disorder (fibrillin) affecting the heart, joints and lungs; reported in a single Golden Retriever puppy carrying one copy of a deletion.

name: Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis 7 (NCL7)
description: A fatal lysosomal storage disease causing progressive loss of vision, coordination and cognition, starting around one year of age. Recessive.

name: Ichthyosis (Golden Retriever type)
description: A scaly-skin disorder: dogs develop flaky, dark scales, usually mild and lifelong. Common in Golden Retrievers; another variant in the same gene occurs in Labradors. Recessive.

name: X-linked retinoschisis (RS1)
description: A candidate cause of splitting of the retinal layers that can impair vision, found in a Pomeranian. X-linked: affected males; females with one copy are carriers.

name: Hyperfibrinolysis (SERPINE1)
description: Blood clots dissolve too quickly, causing spontaneous or post-surgical bleeding; found in English and Welsh Springer Spaniels. Tell your vet before any surgery. Recessive.

name: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (SPAG1)
description: The tiny hairs (cilia) that clear the airways do not beat properly, causing chronic cough, nasal discharge and pneumonia from puppyhood; found in Cocker Spaniels. Recessive.

name: Retinopathy with vitamin E deficiency
description: Low vitamin E causes retinal degeneration and sometimes unsteadiness in English Cocker Spaniels; early vitamin E supplementation may help. Recessive.

name: Menkes-like disease
description: A disorder of copper transport; reported in a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel with kidney (Fanconi) problems, poor growth and incoordination. X-linked: males with one copy are affected.

name: Cone-rod dystrophy (SPATA7)
description: Early loss of day vision (cone-rod dystrophy) in Standard Poodles. Recessive.

name: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (LAMA3)
description: A severe skin-fragility disease: the skin and mouth lining blister and erode at the slightest friction. Recessive.

name: Oculocutaneous albinism
description: Very pale coat, skin and eyes with light sensitivity ('white Doberman' and similar), caused by a pigment transporter defect. Recessive.
